bug_semantics: In pkg/oci/spec_opts.go, WithUser split an OCI image USER value and parsed each UID/GID component with strconv.Atoi, but commit de1341c201ffb0effebbf51d00376181968c8779 changed every parse-or-bound failure—including a syntactically numeric value outside the allowed signed-32-bit range—into the username/group-name lookup path. An attacker-controlled image can therefore use a large decimal USER string such as 2147483648 and supply an /etc/passwd entry with that exact name mapped to UID 0; containerd resolves it as a name and launches as root, bypassing Kubernetes runAsNonRoot expectations.
flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the human-authored security-hardening commit "validate uid/gid" (de1341c201ffb0effebbf51d00376181968c8779). It added min/max UID/GID bounds but coupled out-of-range numeric values to the existing non-numeric-name fallback (`err != nil || v < minUserID || v > maxUserID`) rather than returning an error. That direct code commit is the smallest BIC; 07a0b5419c40 and the release merges/tags are later cherry-pick/landing artifacts, not introducers.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object reports author Craig Ingram <Cjingram@google.com>, committer Craig Ingram <Cjingram@google.com>, and the complete message "validate uid/gid"; the message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer, and neither identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-fqw6-gf59-qr4w states the attack: a numeric USER that cannot be represented under the 32-bit policy is treated as a username, an attacker-supplied /etc/passwd can map that name to root, and runAsNonRoot can be bypassed. It gives affected/patched boundaries >=1.7.27,<1.7.32 (fixed 1.7.32), >=2.0.4,<2.0.9 (fixed 2.0.9), >=2.1.0-beta.0,<2.2.4 (fixed 2.2.4; 2.1 is EOL), and >=2.3.0-beta.0,<2.3.1 (fixed 2.3.1).

BIC commit/API evidence: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/de1341c201ffb0effebbf51d00376181968c8779 and https://api.github.com/repos/containerd/containerd/commits/de1341c201ffb0effebbf51d00376181968c8779. Its pkg/oci/spec_opts.go patch adds math.MaxInt32 bounds and changes the one-component and two-component cases from `if err != nil` to `if err != nil || v < minUserID || v > maxUserID` (and equivalent GID logic), routing the newly rejected numeric range to WithUsername/UserFromPath or group lookup. The same object names its sole parent as 9deb0b8f748ee038dfd48c51d7aee6b55e34e9c1.

Direct-parent verification: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containerd/containerd/9deb0b8f748ee038dfd48c51d7aee6b55e34e9c1/pkg/oci/spec_opts.go in WithUser has no minUserID/maxUserID/minGroupID/maxGroupID constants and only checks `if err != nil`; it lacks the vulnerable bound-failure-to-name conditions. The BIC tree at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containerd/containerd/de1341c201ffb0effebbf51d00376181968c8779/pkg/oci/spec_opts.go contains those conditions. Thus the vulnerable lines are absent in the BIC's immediate parent and first appear in de1341c201ffb0effebbf51d00376181968c8779.

Fix evidence: direct code commit https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/9439355c2bffd12d9e15f1fa57cdd1c6da677cd2 detects strconv.ErrRange and returns explicit `uid out of range`/`gid out of range` errors for parse overflow or values outside the permitted bounds instead of performing name lookup; pkg/oci/spec_opts_user_test.go adds huge numeric UID/GID regression cases. Landing merge https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/ba57862c7b2699f760f01e8d0c31ecbe520e124a has 9439355c2bffd12d9e15f1fa57cdd1c6da677cd2 as its second parent.

reasoning: The advisory's vulnerable behavior is not merely numeric parsing failure: it is the semantic conflation of an out-of-policy numeric identifier with a textual account name. Parent 9deb0b8f748ee038dfd48c51d7aee6b55e34e9c1 did not contain the 32-bit bounds. The code-bearing commit de1341c201ffb0effebbf51d00376181968c8779 introduced those bounds and, in the same smallest change, directed bound failures into username/group resolution. Its later cherry-picks and release merges reproduce but do not originate the flaw, so no squash decomposition is needed. The first affected tags coincide with releases carrying this hardening change. The direct fix 9439355c2bffd12d9e15f1fa57cdd1c6da677cd2 separates numeric range errors from genuinely non-numeric names and was landed by ba57862c7b2699f760f01e8d0c31ecbe520e124a, then backported into every supported patched boundary named by the advisory. Finally, inspection of only the BIC commit object finds a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
